label: The Port Desert

terrain.note: Issue #77: the home planet is a whole ball of sphere_radius metres (src/systems/planets/planet_sphere.gd): sand all the way round, walkable everywhere, up turns with the ground. The flat keys below are what the square desert used and are kept only for worlds without a sphere.

landmarks.note: Wreck field: three more of the same class came down out east, under the Remnant's cruiser and on round toward the far side of the ball, each a couple of km from the last so the next one's stern stands on the horizon. All 'kind': 'wreck' (src/systems/world/starcruiser_wreck.gd). 'variant' makes each barely unique: a different heading, a deck or ramp fallen away, a radiator gone, other railings knocked out (StarcruiserWreck.VARIANT_KEYS). Their droids and the prize crate on each one's bridge platform: droids/droids.json 'wreck'.sites, pickups/port_town.json 'site_crates'.

Issue #295: Skrugs's post, a different place in each town layout ('layouts', resolved once by CoreContent.resolve_layout where the world is loaded). Round port: his yard inside the wall right behind the cantina (skrugs_post_round, turned so +x faces the back lane). Square port: out in the sand past its back gate, where it stood before issue #237 (skrugs_post, +x facing the gate).

Issue #295: Skrugs's sand ramp, out past the back gate (it was part of his post until his round-port yard moved inside the wall). Round port: where it stood when his post was out in the sand. Square port: where it always was, past his post. Rises toward -z.
Issue #187: the four outposts round the other sides of the town, each turned so its door (+x) faces the town.

Issue #193: the Remnant's star cruiser, holding orbit 7 km up over map point 'at' (6.5 km east along the ground, 75 degrees round the ball): below the port's horizon, in plain sight from space. It is level with the port (its decks square to world up, with its own gravity aboard) and its bay is turned toward the port; yaw_deg turns it about its up. 7 km (was 4.6): three km past the edge of space, so the escort fight runs most of the way there. Its shapes are src/systems/world/cruiser_hull.gd, everything else content/core/cruiser/remnant_cruiser.json.

detail.note: Issue #46: less to draw (and run) the higher you fly. Read by src/systems/world/altitude_detail.gd. Each tier holds once the viewer is 'above' that many metres over sea level and lets go 'hysteresis' metres lower. off: render features (sdfgi, ssil, ssao, volumetric, shadows). hide: node groups the town registers (people = bodies, the cantina owner and their brains; props = lamps, banners, boulders). SDFGI goes first: it rebuilds whenever a fast camera moves, which is what made flying laggy.

note: IP-neutral. The world around the port, for flying: where the desert ends and the planet curves away, the landmarks set in it, and the height where the atmosphere ends. The desert's shape is the town's DesertTerrain (src/systems/look/desert_terrain.gd) and its mesas and hoodoos are content/look/desert_landforms.json; this file does not repeat them. terrain.extent = the desert's half-size (its own extent wins when the desert is built); beyond it the ground is skirt_height falling away on a sphere of planet_radius from curve_from. Altitude is measured above that curved surface, so space_altitude is the same everywhere. Issue #46: planet_radius halved (120 km to 60 km), a smaller world whose horizon curves in sooner, so less of it is ever drawn. Colours: content/look/world.json.
